issues.issue: This introductory recital describes the Procedure as reaching only "certain employment-related disputes," while the operative paragraph 1 (c006) binds the associate to arbitrate "any controversy or claim arising out of or relating to your employment relationship." A court could be asked whether the recital's narrower "certain disputes" language controls or is displaced by the operative scope.

The parenthetical condition "after appropriate attempts to resolve your dispute internally through management channels" fixes no standard for what attempts are "appropriate" or when they are exhausted. "Certain disputes" is likewise unbounded on the face of the sentence, leaving the trigger for the arbitration duty indeterminate.

The recited consideration — "your employment as our associate" as a right "to which you are not otherwise entitled" — cannot be squared with the at-will clause (c019), under which employment may be ended at any time and is "not for any specific or definite duration." A court would be asked whether the recited consideration is illusory once the two are read together.

The employer's reciprocal promise to use arbitration as the "exclusive forum" conflicts with the Claims Not Covered clause (c008), which expressly preserves "our" right to seek injunctive and equitable relief, including trade-secret and unfair-competition relief, "from a court of competent jurisdiction." A court could be asked whether the forum is in fact exclusive and mutual.

"After we sign this Agreement" makes execution by both sides a condition precedent to the preclusive effect, yet the signature block bears only a date and a partially rendered "pany Representative" line. Whether the employer ever signed, and whether its signature was required, is squarely raised by these words.

Paragraph 1 commits "any controversy or claim arising out of or relating to your employment relationship" to binding arbitration, which cannot be reconciled with the Claims Not Covered clause (c008) excluding workers' compensation, unemployment, NLRA, EEOC, equitable-relief and benefit-plan claims. A court would have to decide how far "any" is cut back by that exclusion list.

The covered-claims list is introduced by "Includes, but is not limited to" and closed by the catch-all "claims for violation of any federal, state, or other governmental law," so the enumerated specifics give no boundary to the class. The internal qualifier "tort claims (not otherwise exluded)" compounds this by referring outward without identifying what is excluded.

This clause expressly covers "violations of confidentiality or breaches of trade secrets," but c008 carves out claims for injunctive or equitable relief "including without limitation claims for unfair competition and the use or unauthorized disclosure of trade secrets or confidential information." The same trade-secret claim is thus both covered and not covered.

The equitable-relief carve-out opens mutually ("A claim by you or us for injunctive or other equitable relief") but closes unilaterally ("for which we may seek and obtain relief from a court of competent jurisdiction"), so it is unclear whether the employee too may go to court. The surrounding list markers are also garbled ("L", "Iv.", "_A claim"), leaving the enumeration's structure uncertain.

The exclusion of "a claim before the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (or agency with concurrent jurisdiction)" cannot be squared with c007, which commits discrimination claims and "any claim that could be asserted ... before an administrative agency" to arbitration. A court would be asked which governs a statutory discrimination claim.

The prerequisite of "good faith efforts at resolving any dispute internally on an informal basis through our management channels appropriate to that particular dispute" identifies no channel, no time limit and no test for when "those internal efforts fail." Whether the condition has been satisfied — and who decides — is left at large.

This clause conditions arbitration on the dispute remaining unresolved "at the conclusion of the informal procedure as outlined in the Handbook," but the Handbook is neither attached nor incorporated, and c020 declares this Agreement the complete agreement superseding other understandings. A court would have to decide whether the Handbook procedure is part of the bargain at all.

The conflict rule gives the Agreement priority over the AAA rules, yet c010 incorporates those same rules by reference precisely for arbitrator selection and evidence, matters this Agreement addresses only partly. A court would be asked which text supplies the procedure where the Agreement is silent rather than contrary.

Placing the burden of proof "at all times" on the party seeking relief cannot be squared with c013, which directs the arbitrator to apply the governing substantive law, including statutes with their own burden-shifting and affirmative-defense allocations. A court could be asked whether this clause overrides statutory burdens or yields to them.
